correctness.rationale: The unlimited-round ordinary k-pebble strategy preserves occupied components, sides, and injections with at most k-1 survivors; the converse Spoiler strategy uses two retained vertices and a third to distinguish component coalescence and side truncation. Widths 1 and 2 see only equality and adjacency, not three-way component membership. Counting the k choices of truncated n and k(k-1)/2 unordered side pairs gives k²(k-1)/2 theories; the k-threshold establishes order 2k² and identifying width 1+max(n,a,b). Small k=3,4 tests in the package corroborate but are not the proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The matching-deleted biclique theorem is connected and has different edge constraints; the chain-disjoint-union theorem has a transitive order relation, hence not a graph biclique theorem. Generic composition principles remain a priority risk but no concrete theorem deriving the formula was found.
